question: Which of the following Articles of Indian Constitution deals with the election of Vice - President?  (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 1)
options: Article 81
Article 44
Article 66
Article 91
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 66

Explanation:
Article 66 of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice-President. It specifies that the Vice-President shall be elected by members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. The Supreme Court handles any disputes related to the election. Article 63 establishes the office of Vice-President, Article 67 deals with removal, and Article 68 covers vacancy. Note that Article 81 pertains to the composition of Lok Sabha, Article 44 to Uniform Civil Code, and Article 91 to the Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

Explanation:

question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Chief Justice of India
President
Parliament
Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India is appointed by the President. This appointment is made under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, which provides for the establishment and powers of the Election Commission. The President appoints the CEC and other Election Commissioners. The CEC holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. The service conditions of the CEC are similar to those of a Judge of the Supreme Court. The CEC can be removed only through the process of impeachment, similar to a Judge of the Supreme Court. This ensures the independence and impartiality of the Election Commission.

☛ How can the CEC be removed? → Impeachment process

question: Which of the following is known as the lower house of the Indian Parliament? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Lok Sabha
Assembly
Rajya Sabha
Council
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha

Explanation:
The lower house of the Indian Parliament is known as the Lok Sabha. It is directly elected by the people of India. The term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years. Its members are called Members of Parliament (MPs). The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 seats, of which 530 represent states, 20 represent union territories, and 2 are nominated from the Anglo-Indian community. The Lok Sabha has the authority to pass money bills and its presiding officer is the Speaker. The Rajya Sabha is known as the upper house.

question: Which of the following was adopted in the emblem of Government of India from the Maurya dynasty? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Chariot Wheel
Four lions
Horse
The words, 'Satyameva Jayate'
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Four lions

Explanation:
The emblem of Government of India features four lions adopted from the Maurya dynasty. This emblem is derived from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, built by Emperor Ashoka. The four lions stand back to back on a circular abacus, symbolizing power, courage, confidence and pride. The base contains an Ashoka Chakra and other animals. It was officially adopted on 24 January 1950. Other options include chariot wheel, horse, and the words 'Satyameva Jayate', but the central motif is the four lions.

question: Article 40 of the Constitution of India advises the state to work for (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 2)
options: Uniform Civil Code
Constitution of Municipalities
Organisation of Village Panchayats
Prohibition of Child Labour
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Organisation of Village Panchayats

Explanation:
Article 40 of the Constitution of India directs the state to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government. It is one of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV). This provision aims to promote rural development and democratic decentralization. Article 40 is based on Gandhian philosophy, which emphasizes making villages self-reliant. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 later gave constitutional status to panchayats, strengthening this principle further. The directive principles, though non-justiciable, are fundamental in the governance of the country. Article 40 thus guides the state to establish a strong grassroots democracy in rural areas.

question: Who administers the oath of office to the President? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister
Vice-President
Speaker of Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chief Justice of India

Explanation:
The oath of office to the President of India is administered by the Chief Justice of India as per Article 60 of the Constitution. The President swears to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution, uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, and devote themselves to the service of the nation. In the absence of the Chief Justice, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court may administer the oath. The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and state legislative assemblies, using the single transferable vote system. The President holds office for a term of 5 years and can be impeached under Article 61 for violation of the Constitution.

question: Chief Minister of a state is responsible to the- (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (31/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: Legislative Assembly
Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister
Governor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Legislative Assembly

Explanation:
According to Articles 163 and 164 of the Indian Constitution, the Chief Minister of a state assists and advises the Governor, but is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly. This is a fundamental principle of the parliamentary system of government, where the executive (Council of Ministers) is accountable to the legislature. The Chief Minister remains in office as long as he enjoys the majority support in the Legislative Assembly. If a vote of no-confidence is passed in the Assembly, the Chief Minister must resign. The Governor is the constitutional head, but the Chief Minister is not answerable to the Governor; rather, he is responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

question: Can a person be a member of both Houses? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 1)
options: Yes
Yes, during financial emergency
Yes, during a national emergency
No
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is No

Explanation:
According to Article 101 of the Indian Constitution, a person cannot be a member of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) simultaneously. If a person is elected to both Houses, they must resign from one. This provision ensures efficiency and accountability in the functioning of Parliament. This rule applies even during a national emergency or financial emergency, with no exceptions. The principle is also reflected in Articles 102 and 103, which deal with disqualification of membership. Thus, dual membership of both Houses is not permitted. The intention is to prevent conflicts of interest and maintain the integrity of the legislative process. Therefore, the correct answer is 'No'—a person cannot be a member of both Houses at the same time.

question: Generally, the tenure of the members of Lok Sabha is 5 years. But it can be ended earlier as well- (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 1)
options: by the Vice-President
by the prime minister
by the president
by the speaker of the Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is by the president

Explanation:
The normal tenure of Lok Sabha is 5 years, but the power to dissolve it prematurely rests only with the President. As per Article 85(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution, the President can dissolve Lok Sabha at any time. This is usually done when the government loses majority or on the advice of the Prime Minister. However, the President's power is not absolute; he acts on the advice of the Prime Minister, but can use his discretion in certain situations. Upon dissolution, general elections are held. Notably, Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved as it is a permanent house.

question: Which House of the Indian Parliament is more powerful? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 1)

Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
can not be said
Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha

Explanation:
In the Indian Parliament, the Lok Sabha is more powerful because it is directly elected by the people. The Lok Sabha has exclusive authority over money bills, which the Rajya Sabha can only delay for 14 days. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha, and if the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the government must resign. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house but cannot block money bills or remove the government. In constitutional amendments, both houses have equal power, but in ordinary legislation and control over the executive, the Lok Sabha dominates.

question: Can the Rajya Sabha be dissolved? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: never
at the discretion of the President
Yes, every three years
Yes, during an emergency
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is never

Explanation:
The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of the Parliament of India and is a permanent house. This means that the Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved. While the Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President, the Rajya Sabha continues to exist permanently. One-third of its members retire every two years and new members are elected, ensuring its continuity. This feature makes it similar to the US Senate. The main reason for the permanent nature of the Rajya Sabha is that it represents the federal structure and protects the interests of the states.

question: How long did the first national emergency declared in October 1962 last? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: 1977
1965
1968
1966
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1968

Explanation:
The first national emergency in India was declared in October 1962 due to the India-China war. It was proclaimed by the President under Article 352 and continued until the security situation normalized. The emergency was finally revoked in January 1968, lasting about 5 years. During this period, the central government gained extensive powers, and fundamental rights were suspended. This emergency is a significant event in Indian history as it was the first time such a measure was invoked since independence. It also set precedents for the use of emergency powers in later years.
